name: What game are you playing?
description: Start by matching your instrument, time horizon, and decision process.
check: Does the role, holding horizon and invalidation rule match the original mandate?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Instruments, ownership, and hidden claims
description: A familiar price chart can sit on top of a very different legal and economic exposure.
check: What asset or contractual claim is owned, and who controls withdrawal?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Build a survival boundary
description: Money needed for life should not depend on a favorable market path.
check: Is essential money separated from capital that can be lost?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Think in distributions, not certainties
description: A trade has a range of possible outcomes, including outcomes your model omits.
check: Which adverse outcomes are omitted from the forecast?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Build a learning system
description: Study should produce better decisions, not a growing collection of untested opinions.
check: What falsifiable lesson and next observation will this scan produce?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Biases become dangerous through action
description: Naming a bias is useful only if it changes a decision rule.
check: Which written rule interrupts confirmation bias or anchoring?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: FOMO, revenge, and the urgency trap
description: Urgency is a feeling. It is not evidence that a trade is good.
check: Is urgency changing size, entry or stop without new evidence?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Emotion, physiology, and usable judgment
description: Treat internal state as information about decision quality, not as a market signal.
check: Is the operator rested and able to follow the existing plan?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Deliberate practice and the trading journal
description: The journal is an evidence record, not a courtroom for defending the last trade.
check: Was the thesis, expected loss and evidence saved before the outcome?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Crowds, narratives, and reflexive markets
description: A story can influence price without being a reliable valuation model.
check: Is narrative strength supported by observable activity and token economics?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: The auction behind the chart
description: Price is the result of trades and quotes, not a vote on intrinsic value.
check: Are displayed quotes being confused with completed transactions?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Liquidity is multidimensional
description: A market can look busy and still be expensive to exit.
check: Can the intended position exit through the available spread and depth?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Whale activity without mythology
description: Observe actions and constraints; do not pretend to read a large participant's mind.
check: What alternative explanations exist for a large transfer or order?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Read price, volume, OI, and funding together
description: More data helps only when its units, coverage, and limits are understood.
check: Are price, traded volume, OI and funding interpreted with consistent units and times?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Execution is part of the strategy
description: A signal that cannot be traded economically is not a usable retail edge.
check: Do fees, realized slippage and fill quality leave room for the proposed edge?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Decentralized markets and on-chain evidence
description: Removing an intermediary can introduce a different set of execution dependencies.
check: Are pool liquidity, gas, MEV and contract dependencies understood?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Perpetual futures from first principles
description: Understand the payoff before choosing the leverage setting.
check: Are payoff, notional, collateral and contract multiplier explicit?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Mark price, margin, and account structure
description: Liquidation is governed by the venue's risk system, which may use a different price from your chart.
check: Are mark price, maintenance margin and cross/isolated account rules known?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Liquidation cascades and path dependence
description: A forecast about the final price cannot rescue a position that fails on the way there.
check: Would an adverse path liquidate the position before the forecast horizon?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Funding, basis, and the cost of waiting
description: A directional view can be right while the chosen instrument is too expensive to hold.
check: Are funding cash flows and dated-futures basis costs measured separately?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Options, volatility, and convexity
description: Options add dimensions of risk that a directional chart cannot show.
check: Are strike, expiry, settlement, volatility and nonlinear risks specified?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Hedging and residual risk
description: A hedge changes the risk profile; it does not make the position disappear.
check: Can the hedge leg obtain cash when an offsetting gain is inaccessible?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Size from the loss budget
description: Choose the exposure that fits the plan, then check whether the instrument can support it.
check: Is quantity the minimum allowed by planned loss, cash, notional and liquidity constraints?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: R-multiples, expectancy, and drawdown
description: A good performance record describes both reward and the route taken to obtain it.
check: Are net R-multiples calculated from the original risk budget and all trades?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Portfolio risk and correlation
description: Five different tickers can still be one concentrated economic bet.
check: Do different tickers share the same BTC, sector, venue or collateral risks?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Tail risk and stress testing
description: Model what a normal backtest is least likely to teach you.
check: Can the portfolio survive gaps, depegs, illiquidity and unavailable withdrawals?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Stops, scaling, and leverage discipline
description: Every position adjustment is a new decision about exposure.
check: Does every size increase pass a fresh risk review without widening loss limits?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Technical analysis as a testable language
description: A chart pattern becomes useful when its definition survives being written before the outcome.
check: Can the chart pattern be specified before observing its outcome?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Breakouts, fakeouts, and liquidity sweeps
description: A breakout is an event to evaluate, not an instruction to chase.
check: Is the breakout accepted after the boundary, and what would invalidate it?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Trend following and patience
description: A trend strategy tries to participate in persistent moves while accepting repeated failures to start one.
check: Is the trend rule explicit about repeated small failed entries and exit?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Mean reversion and range trading
description: A stretched price is not the same as a mispriced asset.
check: Does mean-reversion evidence survive breaks, costs and unstable relationships?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Build one complete playbook
description: A strategy is a chain of decisions, including when it must stand down.
check: Does the playbook include context, trigger, size, exit and no-trade conditions?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Backtesting without fooling yourself
description: The best historical result is often the one most contaminated by selection.
check: Are fees, slippage, survivorship, look-ahead and all tested variants recorded?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Performance metrics and uncertainty
description: A number becomes meaningful only after its denominator, horizon, and assumptions are stated.
check: Are net returns distinguished from deposits and all metric horizons specified?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Regimes, model risk, and research governance
description: Sophisticated reasoning includes knowing when a model should lose authority.
check: What event would reduce or suspend reliance on the fitted model?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Operations, automation, and incident response
description: A strategy is only as controlled as its worst unattended failure.
check: Are stale feeds, restarts, duplicate notifications and lost state visible?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Build a spot-investment thesis
description: A useful asset can still be a poor investment at a given price or through a given token.
check: Does token ownership capture value even if network usage grows?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Allocation, DCA, and rebalancing
description: A long-term process still needs rules for how much to own and when to reconsider.
check: Are allocation, DCA and rebalance decisions bounded by thesis and capital policy?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Due diligence and the reasons to reject
description: A research process should make it easier to say no.
check: Which missing evidence or concentration is sufficient to reject the asset?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone

name: Think like an investment committee
description: Make the decision defensible before the outcome is visible.
check: Can researcher, skeptic, risk manager and executor defend this decision independently?
status: Manual input required; never inferred from price alone
